questions.prompt: The better night in front of the TV?
questions.bg: The Super Bowl has crowned American football's champion since 1967, one winner-take-all night; the Champions League final has crowned Europe's top club side in a lineage running back to 1956.

questions.prompt: Would you rather win…
questions.bg: Olympic gold arrives once every four years across dozens of sports; football's World Cup, also quadrennial, draws the largest audience of any single sporting event on earth.

questions.prompt: Pure athleticism — rank them
VAR made football better.
questions.bg: Video assistant referees review four things only: goals, penalties, red cards and mistaken identity. Introduced at the 2018 World Cup and in the Premier League from 2019.

questions.prompt: Best sport to watch live in a stadium
E-sports are real sports.
questions.bg: E-sports were a medal event at the 2022 Asian Games, and the IOC has run separate Olympic Esports events since 2021 without adding them to the Olympic programme.

questions.prompt: Your team wins it all — but you can never watch them again. Deal?
One cuisine forever
Milk before cereal is a crime.
Rank the potato formats
Would you eat lab-grown meat?
questions.bg: Cultivated meat is grown from animal cells in a tank, with no slaughter. Singapore approved sale in 2020 and the US in 2023; volumes are tiny and costs still far above farmed meat.

questions.prompt: A free pill replaces all meals. Food becomes hobby-only. Take it?
Final dessert on earth
Spicy food: worth the pain?
The book is always better.
Rank by rewatchability
One world to live in
Watching at 1.5× speed is disrespectful.
The ideal movie length
Spoilers ruin nothing for a good story.
questions.bg: A 2011 University of California study had people read short stories with and without the ending revealed first — the 'spoiled' readers rated the stories slightly higher on average.

questions.prompt: Great lyrics or great melody?
Rank the live music
Vinyl actually sounds better.
questions.bg: Vinyl is analogue: a continuous groove, with surface noise and less dynamic range than digital. Most records since the 1990s are cut from digital masters, so differences owe as much to mastering as to format.

questions.prompt: Music while working?
One decade of music forever
Brain-computer interface, once it’s proven safe?
questions.bg: Brain-computer interfaces read neural signals through implanted electrodes. Trial participants with paralysis have moved cursors and robotic arms and produced speech. The implants require brain surgery and remain research, not products.

questions.prompt: Phones should be banned in schools.
questions.bg: Several countries have restricted phones in schools nationally, others leave it to each school. Studies point both ways: less distraction, but also fewer chances to teach digital habits.

questions.prompt: Which would you give up last?
Delete all your data and start clean, or keep everything forever?
A robot does your chores but records everything. Deal?
Would you ride a driverless taxi tonight?
questions.bg: Driverless taxis carry paying passengers in a handful of cities, with remote operators on standby. They are cleared only inside mapped service areas, and are pulled after incidents.

questions.prompt: Tipping should be abolished.
questions.bg: US federal law lets employers pay tipped staff as little as $2.13 an hour if tips make up the rest. In much of Europe and Japan, service is included in the listed price.

questions.prompt: Ten minutes early or exactly on time?
Rank the perfect weekend
The best age to be
The view from your window, forever
Small talk is a skill, not a chore.
Read minds — but everyone knows you can. Take it?
A million now, but a stranger somewhere loses everything. Press the button?
Would you want to know the date of your death?
Five years in a job you hate, then never work again?
Restart life at 10, everything you know intact?
Perfect memory — but you can never forget anything. Take it?
Your dog talks for one day, or understands you forever?
Should voting be mandatory?
questions.bg: About two dozen countries require voting, and roughly half of those enforce it — Australia and Belgium fine non-voters. Turnout in those countries runs far above comparable voluntary systems.

questions.prompt: Four-day work week: inevitable or fantasy?
questions.bg: Trials in Iceland, the UK and elsewhere cut hours with no cut in pay. Most reported steady output and lower burnout; the trials were small, and mostly office work.

questions.prompt: City centers should be car-free.
questions.bg: Pontevedra, Ghent and Oslo among others have closed their centres to most cars, with permits for residents and deliveries. Measured effects: less traffic and cleaner air, and disputes over shop takings.

questions.prompt: Would you move to another country for good?
Judge the art apart from the artist?
Celebrities should stay out of politics.
Dinner with one
Free will is an illusion.
questions.bg: Determinism holds that every choice follows from prior causes; compatibilism holds that free will can still be real in such a world. Brain studies find activity preceding a reported decision, which both camps read differently.

questions.prompt: We’re not alone in the universe.
questions.bg: Astronomers have confirmed nearly 6,000 planets around other stars, several of them potentially temperate. No evidence of life beyond Earth has been found, and no candidate signal has survived follow-up checks.

questions.prompt: Money can buy happiness.
questions.bg: Studies track income against self-reported wellbeing. A 2010 study found happiness flattening above a middle income; a 2021 one found it still rising slowly at high incomes. Both rest on people rating their own lives.

questions.prompt: Humanity’s best days are ahead.
What matters most — rank them
Doubles or singles?
Pick your surface
Line judges or full electronic calls?
questions.bg: Electronic line calling uses ball-tracking cameras and a recorded voice instead of line judges. The tour has moved towards it since 2020; some events now have no line judges at all.

questions.prompt: Cold water: wetsuit or skin?
questions.bg: Open-water rules commonly mandate wetsuits in cold water and forbid them in warm — World Triathlon draws its lines around 16°C and the low twenties. Ice swimmers race skin in water near freezing.

questions.prompt: Rank the strokes
Pool or open water?
First drafts: longhand or keyboard?
Plot it all, or find it as you write?
Can great writing be taught?
The Ship of Theseus, fully replaced — same ship?
questions.bg: A ship has every plank replaced, one at a time. The puzzle is attributed to Plutarch, writing on the ship of Theseus kept in Athens; it tests what makes a thing the same thing over time.

questions.prompt: Is morality discovered or invented?
questions.bg: Philosophers call the two positions moral realism — moral facts exist and are found — and anti-realism, where morality is something humans construct. Both have serious defenders; neither is settled.

questions.prompt: A perfectly happy simulated life — plug in?
Blitz or classical?
questions.bg: Chess time controls: blitz gives each player 3–5 minutes for the whole game, rapid 10–60, classical 90 minutes or more plus added time. Ratings are kept separately for each.

questions.prompt: Best first move
A draw offer from a stronger player — take it?
Your sourdough starter deserves a name.
Kombucha or kefir?
questions.bg: Both are fermented drinks: kombucha is sweetened tea fermented by a bacteria-and-yeast culture; kefir is milk or water fermented by kefir grains. Kefir carries more microbial strains, kombucha more acid.

questions.prompt: When does old age begin?
questions.bg: Global life expectancy at birth was around 31 in 1900 and is past 73 today. The UN's statistics count 'older persons' from 65; gerontologists increasingly split young-old from old-old at 75.

questions.prompt: The right tip
Daily screen time — where does “too much” start?
questions.bg: Surveys put worldwide daily screen time near seven hours, work included. Formal guidance exists mainly for children — the WHO advises essentially none before age two.

questions.prompt: How much of your life is actually in your control?
Pineapple on pizza — place it
Small talk — place it
AI assistants, today — place them

questions.title: The Wallet
questions.prompt: The Wallet — a wallet, a bus, and nobody watching
questions.intro: The last bus home. On the seat beside you: a wallet, fat with cash. No cameras. No one else aboard.

_.q: It sits there, heavier than it should be.

a.t: Hand it to the driver, unopened

A.q: A student ID. 4,000 in cash. A clinic appointment slip for Thursday.

a.t: Keep the cash, mail the rest back

B.q: The driver shrugs without looking. "Lost box is broken. Your call, friend."

a.t: Take it back — handle it yourself

AA.q: You find them in an hour online. They answer, voice shaking with relief — and offer a reward.

AB.q: A week passes. The clinic slip keeps surfacing in your mind like a splinter.

BA.q: The ID shows an address two streets from yours. Thursday is tomorrow.

BB.q: The doors hiss shut. Through the window you watch the wallet ride away.

a.t: Chase the bus to the next stop

AAA.name: The Quiet Good
AAA.line: No reward, no witness. You did it for the version of you that was watching.

AAB.name: The Honest Trade
AAB.line: Everyone leaves whole. Virtue doesn’t have to be free.

ABA.name: The Long Way Round
ABA.line: The splinter won. Later than right, but right.

ABB.name: Finders, Keepers
ABB.line: The money spent easily. Thursday came and went somewhere else.

BAA.name: The Doorstep
BAA.line: A stranger’s face, changing as they understand. Worth the walk.

BAB.name: By the Book
BAB.line: Clean hands, proper channels. The story ends without your name in it.

BBA.name: The Second Chance
BBA.line: Lungs burning at the next stop. Some choices allow one revision.

BBB.name: Not My Story
BBB.line: You never found out. That was the choice, too.

questions.title: The Wrong Text
questions.prompt: The Wrong Text — a message that was not meant for you
questions.intro: Your boss texts you at 23:40: "Offer the role to the other one. Don’t tell K yet." You are K.

_.q: The message glows in the dark. Typing dots appear, then vanish.

a.t: "I think this wasn’t meant for me."

A.q: Your phone rings ten seconds later. A flustered voice offers "a proper chat tomorrow."

a.t: Take the chat, ask it straight

B.q: Next morning they greet you like nothing happened. The role posting closes Friday.

AA.q: Across the desk they don’t deny it. "The decision wasn’t final," they say. It sounds final.

a.t: Negotiate to stay — on new terms

AB.q: Three interviews in a week. One offer arrives — smaller title, better people.

a.t: Tell your team why you’re going

BA.q: Thursday, empty meeting room. You have the screenshot. They have a story ready.

BB.q: The rival offer lands Friday morning — same pay, a team that actually wanted you.

AAA.name: The Renegotiator
AAA.line: You stayed — but the terms are yours now, and everyone knows it.

AAB.name: The Clean Exit
AAB.line: Shortest resignation letter in company history. No regrets by Tuesday.

ABA.name: The Whistle
ABA.line: The team heard the truth. Some doors close loudly and that’s fine.

ABB.name: The Quiet Departure
ABB.line: No scene, no speech. Your absence said it.

BAA.name: Cards on the Table
BAA.line: The screenshot did the talking. Their face did the confessing.

BAB.name: The Poker Face
BAB.line: You never showed your hand. They folded anyway.

BBA.name: The Better Door
BBA.line: Monday, new desk. The old boss still doesn’t know you knew.

BBB.name: The Long Game
BBB.line: You stayed with the receipts. Leverage keeps better than anger.

questions.prompt: ABBA or Queen?
questions.bg: ABBA: Swedish pop quartet, Eurovision winners in 1974, ten years together and a 2021 reunion album. Queen: British rock band fronted by Freddie Mercury, from Bohemian Rhapsody to the 1985 Live Aid set.

questions.prompt: Who left the bigger mark: Einstein or Shakespeare?
questions.bg: Albert Einstein rewrote physics with special and general relativity (1905, 1915) and won the 1921 Nobel Prize. William Shakespeare wrote some 37 plays and 154 sonnets that four centuries of theatre keep staging.

questions.prompt: How many years until a human walks on Mars?
questions.bg: Twelve people have walked on the Moon, the last in 1972, and nobody has travelled farther since. A Mars crew would spend six to nine months in transit each way; official ambitions name the 2030s at the earliest.

questions.prompt: The right way to see a film?
Let AI write your texts for you?
Is a hot dog a sandwich?
questions.bg: Merriam-Webster's dictionary reckons a hot dog fits its sandwich definition — a filling between bread. The US National Hot Dog and Sausage Council formally disagrees, calling it a category of its own.

questions.prompt: The music you loved at 15 — still good, or evidence?
Marie Curie or Ada Lovelace — whose name should more kids know?
questions.bg: Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences for her work on radioactivity — still the only person to have done so. Ada Lovelace's 1843 notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine contain what is widely counted the first published computer program.

questions.prompt: Subtitles on, even in your own language?
Should social media have a minimum age of 16?
questions.bg: Australia legislated a minimum age of 16 for social media accounts in 2024, the first country to do so. The usual platform minimum of 13 traces to a 1998 US children's-privacy law.

questions.prompt: Breakfast: the same thing every day, or never the same?
At what age is an athlete past their peak?
questions.bg: Sports science places most athletic peaks between 25 and 30 — sprinters earlier, endurance athletes and goalkeepers later. Tom Brady won a Super Bowl at 43; gymnasts have won world titles at 16.

questions.prompt: Mozart or Beethoven?
questions.bg: Mozart (1756–1791) wrote more than 600 works — operas, symphonies, the unfinished Requiem — in a 35-year life. Beethoven (1770–1827) bridged the classical and romantic eras and composed his late masterpieces, the Ninth Symphony among them, after going deaf.

questions.prompt: Would you take fame, if it were offered?
The best seat in the cinema?
Should the Olympics settle in one permanent home?
questions.bg: The modern Games have rotated hosts since 1896. Recent editions have run billions over budget, and a fixed site — Athens is the perennial candidate — gets proposed after nearly every expensive Games.

questions.prompt: How many coffees a day is too many?
questions.bg: Europe's food-safety authority puts routine caffeine intake up to 400 mg a day — roughly four to five cups of coffee — within safe limits for healthy adults, and half that in pregnancy.

questions.prompt: Would you live forever, if you could?
How long should a concert be?
Dinner with Napoleon, or with Cleopatra?
questions.bg: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804, redrew Europe's map and laws, and fell at Waterloo. Cleopatra VII ruled Egypt for two decades as its last pharaoh, allied by turns with Caesar and Mark Antony.

questions.prompt: Watch the trailer first, or go in blind?
Election night: up late for the count, or read it in the morning?
Cake or pie?
Penalty shootouts: great drama, or a cruel coin flip?
questions.bg: The World Cup's first shootout came in 1982, and the 1994 final between Brazil and Italy was the first settled by one. Antonín Panenka won Euro 1976 with the chipped penalty that still bears his name.

questions.prompt: One instrument, mastered overnight — which?
Meet your hero — or keep the myth?
Trailers before the film — how many minutes is right?
A total eclipse nearby — travel to stand in it?
questions.bg: In a total eclipse the Moon covers the Sun completely for a few minutes and day drops to twilight. For any single spot on Earth, totality passes overhead roughly once in 375 years.

questions.prompt: Cold leftovers the next morning: better, or sad?
Paper books or an e-reader?
The saddest instrument?
One painting for your wall: Frida Kahlo, or Picasso?
questions.bg: Frida Kahlo painted unsparing self-portraits threaded with Mexican folk imagery, much of it from bed after a bus crash at eighteen. Pablo Picasso co-invented Cubism and left tens of thousands of works, Guernica among them.

questions.prompt: End credits: sit through them, or straight out?
New Year's Eve: the big night, or asleep by eleven?
How many close friends does a person need?
Soup: a meal, or a starter?
Trump has labelled the Strait of Hormuz new US territory. Your read?
questions.bg: The Strait of Hormuz is the 33-kilometre channel between Iran and Oman that every tanker leaving the Gulf has to pass through. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil moves across it. The water is Iran's and Oman's; ships cross under the transit-passage right in the Law of the Sea.

questions.prompt: Crude is near $94. Has the pump changed how you get around?
questions.bg: Crude is the raw barrel, not the pump price. In much of Europe more than half of what you pay at the forecourt is tax and duty, with refining and retail margin on top, so a move in the crude price arrives diluted and several weeks late.

questions.prompt: Evergrande's founder got life for fraud and bribery. That sentence is…
questions.bg: Evergrande was China's largest property developer by sales, financed by pre-selling flats that were not yet built. It defaulted on its offshore debt in 2021 owing more than $300bn, and a Hong Kong court ordered it liquidated in January 2024, leaving unfinished towers across the country.

questions.prompt: Harry and Meghan move back to Britain, but keep no royal duties. Workable?
questions.bg: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back from working royal duties in January 2020 and moved to California. They kept their titles and gave up what came with the roles: the public engagements, the Sovereign Grant funding, and publicly funded security in the UK.

questions.prompt: A model published proofs for ten open problems in maths. Is that doing maths?
questions.bg: An open problem is one nobody has solved. A proof counts only once others can check it — by refereeing, or by writing it in a proof assistant like Lean that verifies each step mechanically. Computers have settled proofs before: the four-colour theorem went that way in 1976.

options.label: Not until a human gets it

questions.prompt: Italy's fourth heatwave this summer, red alerts in 25 cities. Just summer now?
questions.bg: Italy's health ministry grades heat city by city on a three-level scale, and red is the top one: the heat is rated a risk to everyone, not only to the old and the ill. Attribution studies find warming has made heatwaves of a given severity both more frequent and more intense.

questions.prompt: One more work from a lost genius: Mozart, or Van Gogh?
questions.bg: Mozart died at 35 with his Requiem unfinished on the desk. Van Gogh died at 37, having painted nearly 900 canvases in a single decade and sold almost none of them in his lifetime.

questions.prompt: Karaoke: joy, or ordeal?
A film you love gets a remake — excited, or bracing?
Daylight saving time: keep it, or scrap it?
questions.bg: Daylight saving began as a coal-saving measure in the First World War. The European Parliament voted in 2019 to end the twice-yearly change, but member states never settled which time to keep, so the clocks still move.

questions.prompt: How many hours a day on a phone is too many?
Know exactly what people think of you — would you?
Whose biography tonight: Churchill, Bowie, Serena Williams, or Marie Curie?
questions.bg: Churchill led Britain through the Second World War and won a Nobel Prize in Literature. Bowie reinvented pop across five decades. Serena Williams took 23 Grand Slam singles titles. Curie won Nobels in two different sciences.

questions.prompt: The song stuck in your head: fight it, or play it?
Tonight's film: a favourite again, or a gamble on something new?
World Cup final: in the stadium, at home with friends, or the big screen in a pub?
Books finished last year — how many?
Pineapple on pizza?
questions.bg: Hawaiian pizza — ham and pineapple — was invented in 1962 by Sam Panopoulos, a Greek-born cook in Chatham, Ontario, Canada, and named after the brand of canned pineapple he used.

questions.prompt: The narrator of your life's documentary: David Attenborough, or Morgan Freeman?
questions.bg: David Attenborough has narrated British natural history broadcasting since the 1950s, from Life on Earth to Planet Earth. Morgan Freeman's narration runs from The Shawshank Redemption to March of the Penguins.

questions.prompt: Your funeral song: make them cry, or make them dance?
Laugh-track sitcoms: cosy, or unbearable?
A single world holiday, everyone off on the same day: dream, or nightmare?
Hours of live sport in a good week?
Your life's photos: in the cloud, or on a drive you can hold?
Whose diary would you rather read?
How old were you when your taste in music settled?
Watching a film in pieces over a week?
Human nature — place it
Lending a favourite book?
Artefacts taken long ago, sitting in faraway museums?
questions.bg: Museums have begun returning contested holdings — Germany sent Benin Bronzes back to Nigeria in 2022, and talks over the Parthenon Marbles continue. The universal-museum position holds that one collection shows objects to more of the world.

questions.prompt: A new statue for your town square: an artist, a scientist, an athlete, or nobody?
Live album, or studio album?
Meals cooked from scratch in a week?
Cinema snacks: essential, or a racket?
Your team is losing badly. Stay to the end, or beat the traffic?
Voice messages: a gift, or a burden?
Which expedition would you have joined?
A song you love turns up in an ad: ruined, or fair play?
If no one would ever know what you did, would you act differently?
Handwritten letters: bring them back, or let them go?
Voting at 16: about time, or too young?
The ideal dinner hour?
A stranger's kindness you still remember: tell them, or leave it?
The villain everyone secretly roots for: fine, or a problem?
Learning an instrument at 40: worth starting, or too late?
Watching sport alone, or in a crowd?
Your search history, visible to one person you trust: fine, or absolutely not?
How many years ahead do you actually plan?
The famous person you'd trust to babysit: Dolly Parton, Keanu Reeves, David Attenborough, or Michelle Obama?
Minutes late before it counts as late?
Never lie again — and never be lied to. Take the deal?
A referendum on every big question: more democracy, or chaos?
Breakfast: sweet, or savoury?
Black-and-white films: a treat, or a chore?
The band re-forms without its singer: still the band, or a tribute act?
The teacher you'd want for one term: Aristotle, Leonardo da Vinci, Charles Darwin, or Maya Angelou?
The Olympics: summer, or winter?
Video calls: camera on, or camera off?
What writes more of a life: luck, or effort?

questions.title: The Reunion
questions.prompt: The Reunion — twenty years, one evening
questions.intro: Twenty years since the last day of school. The invitation has sat in your inbox for a week; the RSVP closes at midnight.

_.q: Midnight is an hour away. The form wants one click.

A.q: You arrive early. Across the room: your old best friend, mid-laugh, twenty years older.

a.t: Get a drink, read the room first

B.q: Next morning the group chat fills with photos. Someone writes: "Where were you?"

a.t: The truth — crowds aren't your thing
Say work got in the way

AA.q: An hour in, no time has passed at all. They mention they're moving back next month.

a.t: Set a date and a place, tonight

AB.q: From your corner the room sorts itself into its old tables. Your old friend spots you and waves.

BA.q: A private reply: "Fair. I only went hoping you'd be there."

a.t: Offer a coffee, just you two

BB.q: The chat moves on. One tagged photo shows your old table — someone new in your old seat.

AAA.name: The One Who Books It
AAA.line: A date, a place, no 'sometime'. Twenty years turned out to be a scheduling problem.

AAB.name: The Warm Maybe
AAB.line: The hug was real. The 'sometime' stayed a sometime.

ABA.name: The Late Arrival
ABA.line: 'Almost didn't come' — said out loud, it became the best story of the night.

ABB.name: The Observer
ABB.line: You saw the whole evening clearly. It never quite saw you.

BAA.name: The Two-Chair Table
BAA.line: No name tags, no speeches. The reunion that actually reunited.

BAB.name: The Door Ajar
BAB.line: Warm, unanswered. Some doors you like exactly this open.

BBA.name: The Midnight Scroller
BBA.line: Every photo, twice. You attended after all — from here.

BBB.name: The Clean Break
BBB.line: The chat went quiet because you asked it to. So did the decade.

questions.prompt: Teleport anywhere instantly — but you can never travel slowly again. Take it?
A cashless world: convenient future, or something lost?
Ketchup: fridge, or cupboard?
One genre forever: comedy, thriller, drama, or documentary?
How many songs on a perfect album?
One selfie with: Beyoncé, the Pope, Lionel Messi, or Taylor Swift?
Nine-figure transfer fees: the market working, or football losing the plot?
questions.bg: Europe's summer transfer window closed on 1 September. Deadline day brought a rush of deals across the big leagues, several at nine-figure fees, before squads lock until the winter window opens in January.

questions.prompt: A $4bn telescope just left to hunt dark energy. Money well spent?
questions.bg: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy on 30 August, bound for the L2 point 1.5 million kilometres out. Its wide-field camera will hunt exoplanets and map dark energy; the mission cost about $4.3 billion.

options.label: Ask me when it finds something

questions.prompt: A Grand Slam without the world No. 1: wide open, or missing something?
questions.bg: The 2026 US Open runs 30 August to 13 September in New York. Top-ranked Jannik Sinner withdrew before play began with a knee injury; Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka arrived as the defending singles champions.

questions.prompt: Awards season opens at Venice. Do festival prizes change what you watch?
questions.bg: The 83rd Venice International Film Festival runs 2 to 12 September and opens the autumn awards season. Maggie Gyllenhaal chairs the main-competition jury; 21 world premieres compete for the Golden Lion.
